chunks: And from the report of Dirar ibn Hamzah al-Dabbi when he entered upon Muawiya, and his asking him about the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him),

he said: I bear witness that I have seen him on some of his occasions, when night had spread its curtains, and he was standing in his niche (prayer place), holding his beard, groaning like a healthy man (or: like one bitten by a snake), weeping as a grieving man weeps, and saying:

key_terms.السَّلِيمِ: the healthy one (or: like a snakebite)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali (peace be upon him) behave during his night prayers?
ai.summary: This vivid narrative from Nahj al-Balagha captures Ali ibn Abi Talib’s profound spiritual presence during night prayers, emphasizing his asceticism and emotional connection with God. The imagery of him holding his beard and weeping reflects the Shia tradition of valuing deep introspection and humility in worship. This scene underscores the concept of 'zuhd' (renunciation of worldly desires) as a means to attain closeness to Allah.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 77. It is related that when Ḍirār ibn Ḥamzah (the correct: Ḍamrah) aḍ-Ḍibābī (or aṣ-Ṣudā’ī) [1] went to Mu‘āwiyah, and Mu‘āwiyah enquired from him about Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him,

he said: I stand witness that I have seen him on several occasions when night had spread and he was standing in the niche (of the mosque) holding his beard, groaning like a man bitten by a snake and weeping as a grieved man, saying:
